notes:
Account summary: enterprise logistics platform handling real-time shipment routing and marketplace matching. Interest in Dedicated for predictable throughput and private VPC control. Main asks: 99th pct latency <= 120ms for 1k concurrent chat sessions (prompt+response), guaranteed baseline throughput 60k tokens/sec for reranking pipeline, and ability to reserve 8 GPUs for daily peak windows.

Call highlights (03/02 meeting):
- Product: demo of dedicated pool and autoscale knobs; customer impressed with prefix caching idea.
- Security: requires SOC2 evidence plus KMS integration; strict data residency for EU customers (subset of corp).
- Ops: prefer deterministic billing (reserved + burst) and SLA that includes p99 latency targets and credit model.
- Quote from CTO: "We cannot have variance during peak windows — three second tail is a dealbreaker."

Informal feedback: wants a deterministic plan for warm KV caches across restarts, and an artifact showing sustained throughput over a 24h soak with representative workload. They pushed on worst-case cold-starts for large context lengths (8k tokens).

poc_scope:
Objective: validate Dedicated capacity for customer SLA commitments. Scope includes:
- Throughput target: baseline sustained 60k tokens/sec for reranking micro-batches (beam rerank), scale-to-peak 200k tokens/sec with burst policy.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 35ms, p95 < 90ms, p99 <= 120ms for chat (avg prompt length 120 tokens, response 220 tokens) under 1k concurrent sessions.
- Cold-start/restore test: simulate node restarts causing KV cache rebuilds; measure tail latency and recovery time.
- Soak test: 7-day soak to surface memory leaks and degradation; daily maintenance window simulation.
- Representative prompts: 1) short routing query (10-30 tokens), 2) context-heavy policy synthesis (2.5k token context), 3) reranking set of 250 items (embedding+model scoring).
- Metrics collected: token/sec, active concurrent requests, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU util, I/O wait, memory footprint, KV cache hit ratio, cost per 1M tokens.
- Reserved capacity plan: propose initial commit 8xA100-80GB equivalent (dedicated pool), with autoscale burst to +50% for 4 hours/day during peak.
poc_findings_summary:
Summary from initial tests (3/09):
- Warm steady-state: 4xA100 equiv delivered ~68k tokens/sec sustained for rerank micro-batches; p95 latency 82ms for chat; p99 around 138ms (slightly above target).
- Cold restart impact: p99 spikes up to 2.1s for first 2 minutes while KV caches repopulate. Need pre-warm steps or rolling restarts.
- Memory: observed 5% growth over 24h on baseline config; SE suspects an edge case in batching layer — follow-up with infra team.
- Cost estimate: Reserved 8 GPU commit reduces per-token cost by ~32% vs on-demand; burst pricing model required to stay within budget.
- Action items: run 7-day soak on full 8xA100 pool, implement warmup script, tune batching window to reduce variance.
sla_negotiation_notes: Customer requests SLA with explicit latency SLOs tied to credits. Proposed Redwood clause: credit if monthly p99 exceeds 120ms for more than 3% of requests. Customer pushing for 1% window and higher credit. Legal redlines expected around incident definitions and acceptable maintenance windows. Need to align on: scheduled maintenance windows, emergency maintenance, and RTO for escalations (30m during incidents).
technical_blockers:
- Network egress/peering policy; customer wants private peering into their VPC.
- KMS pinning for model keys in private deployment — requires integration work and testing.
- Cold-start tail — architecture decision: pre-warm vs always-on keepalive increases cost.
